newsitem.title: UK: Funds less bullish on Japan equities - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Funds less bullish on Japan equities - Merrill.

text.p: Japanese fund managers are less bullish about prospects for domestic equities due to recent choppy economic data and related earnings forecast downgrades, said a survey by Merrill Lynch.

"Optimism about the Japanese equity market appears to have peaked last month," the survey said. The July survey found fewer respondents were bullish on the outlook for the market on a three or 12 month view.
As a result, managers were less keen to raise their weighting in the Japanese equity market, with buyers outnumbering sellers by 33 percent -- the lowest level since March.
It said the average EPS growth forecast for 1997 was 9.3 percent against 10.3 percent previously, and for 1998 8.1 percent against June's 9.3 percent.
It said around 80 percent of respondents were expecting higher bond yields and a higher discount rate. The risk is perceived to stem from increasing activity rather than inflation.
They were negative on the outlook for the banking and securities sectors, while manufacturing and telecommunications were liked.
The survey was carried out between July 7 and 8, covering 41 institutions responsible for funds totalling $640 billion.
